title: MBE
brief_context: Author of the article regarding the Women's Advisory Committee.
brief_extract:
4 Million Women can't be wrong! by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Director, EAW
TWENTY-ONE years ago this March the first meeting of the Women's Advisory Committee of the British Standards Institution took place. The WAC as it is now commonly called, was set up on the recommendation of the Cunliffe Committee which had been appointed in 1949 by the then President of the Board of Trade to enquire into the organisation and constitution of the BSI.

brief_context: Mentioned as the chair of a committee recognizing WAC's value.
article_title: The Women's Advisory Committee (WAC) of the British Standards Institution (BSI)
brief_extract: The WAC is represented on a Home Office Working Party which has been considering whether and if so how the Regulations can be extended to cover other garments and to material sold by the yard. One of the values of WAC representatives on technical committees is, as the Cunliffe Committee recognised, that they are able to draw attention to some of the hazards in the home and some of the shortcomings on the part of users which are not always apparent to technologists. Unfortunately there can be no standard for the careful user, and it is important, therefore, that design standards should pay particular attention to the safety aspect and that tests for household equipment should simulate as closely as possible some of the accidents that can all too readily occur in the home.

title: King
brief_context: The monarch during whose reign Rudding Park was built.
brief_extract: It takes hardly an hour in a car to reach Whernside, the peak where the River Nidd has its source; and the ancient town of Knares- borough, with its romantic castle overlooking the last gorge of the Nidd before it flows into the plain of York, is not four miles away. There is a choice of stately homes: Rudding Park, literally on Harrogate's doorstep, built in the reign of William IV and set in a Capability Brown park; Harewood House, nine miles away, a treasure-house of Chippendale masterpieces; Newby Hall, near Ripon, with its Gobelin tapestries, and, farther afield, Bramham Park's Versailles style gardens and Castle Howard, a monument to Vanbrugh's genius. And, of course, there is an ever wonderful Fountain Abbey at Studley, near Ripon, which ancient city has its own treasures, among them a fine cathedral, and again farther afield but easily reached the restored glories of York Minster and the abbeys of Byland, Jervaulx and Coverham.

brief_context: Author of the article on air conditioning in Britain.
article_title: Air Conditioning Prospects in Great Britain
brief_extract:
Air Conditioning Prospects
in Great Britain
by ROBERT POLLARD, CENG, MIEE, The Electricity Council

AIR conditioning is essential to comfortable living in countries like the United States because without it the very high summer temperatures make indoor living conditions quite intolerable. In Britain, many still consider it to be an expensive luxury, made unnecessary by the ‘temperate’ British climate; but in view of the much higher humidity conditions which exist in this country it is just as essential here.

title: FIHVE
brief_context: Managed the national Air Conditioning Advisory Bureau in London.
brief_extract: Nearly two years ago the Electricity Council set up a national Air Conditioning Advisory Bureau at 2 Charing Cross (Northumberland Avenue), London, SW1. Managed by Bernard Hough, FIHVE, the primary aim of the Bureau is to stimulate interest in and awareness of the benefits of air conditioning in commercial and industrial premises. Potential users can obtain information and advice on the type of installation which will best suit their requirements.

title: Dr
brief_context: Stressed the importance of formal education for African women.
brief_extract: While it has long been recognised as essential in industry it is now part and parcel of commercial life and women have come to realise that they must have 'know-how' of the right kind to succeed in their professional careers and to run their homes to best advantage. In her Caroline Haslett Memorial Trust Lecture on Nation Building and the African Woman Dr Letitia Obeng stressed that the acquisition of the relevant 'know-how' through formal education was a necessity for women to play their full part. As she stated, without it even a queen-mother in Ghana with all her traditional power, her sophistication and business astuteness could not participate effectively in policy-making decisions.

article_title: A British Woman at Harvard Business School
brief_extract:
A British Woman at Harvard Business School
by JEAN GOMM, bursary holder of the Caroline Haslett Memorial Trust

“WHAT’S a nice girl like you doing in a place like this?” a question frequently asked by both fellow students and companies who come to interview on the campus of Harvard Business School in America. I find that it does seem strange to many and requires explanation that a 25-year-old English girl should be studying for a Master’s Degree in Business Administration at the world’s No 1 Management School.

brief_context: The author reflecting on her experiences as a female student.
brief_extract: There is also the problem of adapting to one's environment and finding a position which feels comfortable without becoming 'one of the boys' or the 'class pet'. One male colleague ceased calling me Jeannie instead of Jean (which always made me feel as if I was being patted on the head for being a good girl) when I started to refer to him as Kennie. I also find that I react in other ways.

brief_extract:
Northern Lands

by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Director, EAW

Market Place, Helsinki

MEMORIES crowd in on me as I try to record my impressions of Finland, of the International Congress on Home Economics which I recently attended there and of the brief visit I paid to Leningrad, that most beautiful of northern cities. At the International Congress there were nearly 1000 delegates from 43 countries, including 133 from the United Kingdom.

brief_extract: The Finnish Association of Electricity Supply Undertakings was most kind to those of us with electrical interests and entertained us on several occasions. We were particularly indebted to Mrs Tamminen, the Publicity Officer, for all the trouble she took to arrange some fascinating expeditions for us. On one afternoon we were taken to have a meal at the home of a doctor and his wife, the latter having worked for the Association before her marriage.

brief_context: Sent to Bristol to buy his wines in Norman times.

The Port of Bristol
Bristol has a long history as a centre of the wine trade both as a port and as the home of great merchants. In Norman times it was a wine producing area and King John sent to Bristol to buy his wines. Bristol has had close links with the European wine producing areas since the 12th century when the marriage of Henry II to Eleanor of Aquitaine added to the English continental possessions many of the finest wine-growing districts in France.

brief_context: Noted American author of Folk Medicine mentioned regarding cider vinegar.
brief_extract: Apart from its culinary uses, the attributes of cider vinegar as an aid to slimming should not be overlooked. With one fluid ounce of Martlet vinegar containing less than one calorie, two teaspoons taken in water twice daily after meals should, according to Dr Jarvis the noted American author of Folk Medicine, result in the reduction of at least 1" round the waistline every two months. Recently there has been a tremendous demand, particularly in Scandinavian countries, for the 50/50 blend of cider vinegar and unpasteurised honey, marketed by Merrydown as Honegar.

title: Dowager Lady
brief_context: A trophy named after her was won by Enfield Branch.
article_title: VISIT TO BELLING & CO LTD, BURNLEY WORKS
brief_extract:
MONTAGUE, Magazine Secretary, Enfield Branch

This is the Diamond Jubilee year of Belling & Co Ltd, and also the 10th Anniversary of the Enfield Branch. To mark these two events and the Branch success in winning the Dowager Lady Swaythling Trophy the Chairman and Managing Director, Mr Richard Belling, arranged a visit by air to these works where Belling electric heaters are manufactured. Steel, aluminium, brass and chrome are all used in the production of the heaters and the quality of all metals is strictly controlled.

title: King
brief_context: Granted the first Royal warrant to the crystal works.
article_title: VISIT TO THE ROYAL BRIERLEY CRYSTAL WORKS, BRIERLEY HILL
brief_extract: The factory was remodelled in 1949 and has the most up-to-date equipment and a glass melting capacity of 30 pots or crucibles. The first Royal warrant was granted by King George V and visits have been made by our present Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip, also King George VI and the Queen Mother and other members of the Royal family. Members saw the glassware being made, starting with the ‘Batch’, silica, lead, potassium and broken glass mixed, then melted in crucibles arranged round circular furnaces, and re-heated to approximately 1,400°C thus becoming molten and clarified glass.
